message.what: A geomagnetic sudden impulse has been observed, indicating the arrival of a coronal mass ejection-driven disturbance.
message.observed: The sudden impulse was observed at 1645 UTC Fri May 10 2024 following detection of an interplanetary shock in the upstream solar wind at 1639 UTC Fri May 10 2024.
message.basis: This alert is based on real-time upstream solar wind measurements and observations from the ground-based magnetometer network available at 1647 UTC Fri May 10 2024.
message.current_status: Solar wind conditions are becoming strongly enhanced following shock arrival. Geomagnetic activity is expected to increase as the disturbance moves past Earth. A Space Weather Warning remains in effect for G3-G5 conditions.
message.future_alerts: This alert confirms arrival of the coronal mass ejection-driven disturbance. Additional Observed Space Weather Alerts will be issued when geomagnetic activity first reaches G3, G4, or G5.
message.impacts: The sudden impulse may produce rapid magnetic-field changes and marks the beginning of potentially significant geomagnetic activity. Power grid, satellite, GNSS, HF radio, and other magnetically sensitive operations should prepare for worsening conditions.
message.precautionary_preparedness_actions: Partners should begin heightened monitoring, follow sector-specific procedures, and monitor SWPC Warning Updates, Observed Space Weather Alerts, and decision-support guidance.
